summary: The now() mutation is only half-pinned: no test covers the open-side clock_timestamp() in windowOpen

comments.author: agent
comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
Filed from TKT-274's fourth ai-review pass as an **incidental** finding — outside that ticket's comment-only scope, so it was recorded in the code comment and split out here rather than fixed in place.

Verified at HEAD, not inherited from the review:
- `windowOpen` has two `clock_timestamp()` occurrences (`channel_allocations.go:43-44`).
- `TestWindowPredicateDecidesAtDecisionTimeNotTransactionStart` (`:697`) sets `opens_at` to NULL, so only the close-side occurrence is exercised.

Needs shaping before Gate 1.

description:
Incidental, found by the fourth adversarial review pass on TKT-274 (a comment-only ticket) and verified against the code.

`windowOpen` (`services/inventory/internal/store/channel_allocations.go:43`) contains **two** `clock_timestamp()` occurrences:

```sql
(opens_at IS NULL OR opens_at <= clock_timestamp())
AND (closes_at IS NULL OR closes_at > clock_timestamp())
```

`TestWindowPredicateDecidesAtDecisionTimeNotTransactionStart` (`channel_allocations_smoke_test.go:697`) is the test that pins "the predicate decides at DECISION time, not transaction-start time" — the `now()`-for-`clock_timestamp()` mutant. It works by holding a transaction open across the cutoff, so frozen `now()` and moving `clock_timestamp()` diverge.

But it sets `opens_at` to **NULL** and only makes `closes_at` cross the gap. So it exercises **only the close-side occurrence**. A per-occurrence mutation of the **open-side** `clock_timestamp()` to `now()` leaves it green.

## Why it matters

The open side is not symmetric decoration. A window written with `now()` on `opens_at` decides "has the sale opened?" at **transaction-start** time. A hold that queues on the pool lock before the on-sale instant and acquires it after would read the frozen start time and be refused as not-yet-open — or, with a transaction that began before the boundary, admitted early. That is the same class of bug ADR-024 litigated for `release_at`, on the side that governs **on-sale**, which is the highest-contention moment in the system.

## Scope

- [ ] Add a transaction-held case with a non-NULL `opens_at` that opens DURING the held transaction, asserting the shipped predicate says OPEN while frozen `now()` says not-yet-open (the mirror of the existing close-side case, including its "fixture did not reproduce the divergence" guard).
- [ ] Mutate the OPEN-side `clock_timestamp()` alone to `now()` and observe the new case go red — the mutation that is evidence is the one only this case can catch. Confirm the existing close-side case stays green under that mutation, which is what demonstrates the gap was real.
- [ ] Update the TKT-274 comment block: it currently records this gap as open ("only PARTLY pinned... a mutation of the OPEN-side occurrence alone would stay green"). Close that wording when the test lands.

## Notes

TKT-274 recorded the gap in the comment rather than closing it, because that ticket was comment-only by scope. The wording there is deliberately explicit so the gap is on the record rather than implied shut — do not delete it without adding the test.

Not `risk:low` on its face: the deliverable is a test, but its central question is "how do I construct a fixture that can actually fail?", which is the shape AGENTS.md says to keep the plan gate for (the TKT-266 precedent). The existing close-side case is a working template, which argues the other way. Let shaping settle it.
